summary: The startup config file templating system has silent failure modes due to fragile comment-based detection of the # enable-template marker; the proposal is to always render files through Sprig to eliminate bugs and reduce code complexity.
userImpact: Users configuring Temporal Server can experience silent failures when config templating is unintentionally disabled due to typos or placement issues with the enable-template marker, leading to template variables not being resolved.
rootCause: The template enabling check uses fragile comment detection (substring search for # enable-template within first 1KB) instead of a more robust mechanism.
proposedFix: Always render config files through Go/Sprig template engine since plain YAML passes through unchanged; alternatively use .yaml.tmpl extension or explicit flag/env var.
keyQuote: Always render config files through the Go/Sprig template engine. Plain YAML passes through unchanged.
